**Finding: Deviation (medium, commercial) — MFN running against us.**

- **§ 7.2 (p0026)** is a reverse MFN: it requires *Customer* to disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives before engaging another provider. That is the walk-away position under the MFN rule — an open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to the Vendor — and it would also force disclosure of our other suppliers' pricing.
- It contradicts **§ 12.3 (p0044)**, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment.
- No Vendor-granted MFN exists anywhere in the document, so nothing beneficial to us is lost by deletion.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** delete § 7.2 in full — the minimal edit that reaches the preferred position, with the 12-month/defined-product matching right offered as a fallback in the comment.
